sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Per-deployment brand settings file
sections.what: Holds the settings that make shared code specific to one deployment. A user does not see this file directly; its effects appear in taxonomy and Opportunity Map output.
sections.why: The header says it is per side so that each deployment can have its own details, and that two copies of shared/industries.ts import it.
sections.watch_out: Each artifact has its own copy, so a change made in one does not reach the other.

sections.name: BRAND_TAXONOMY_FIRMS
sections.title: Extra consulting firm segmentations
sections.what: An empty list of extra consulting firm segment names that shared code can use to extend the firm taxonomy. Nothing is added in this copy, so anything that depends on these names is empty.
sections.why: The comment says these are extra segmentations named in the taxonomy note. The reason beyond that is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Because the list is empty by default, a deployment that forgets to fill it in will see no extra firm segments.

sections.name: BRAND_TAXONOMY_SOURCES
sections.title: Extra taxonomy sources and blocked names
sections.what: Holds an empty set of extra taxonomy sources, which would be merged into the main source list, and one pattern that blocks the word bane in Opportunity Map output, ignoring capital letters. In this copy nothing extra is merged, and the only active filter is that one word.
sections.why: The comment says consultancy names must never appear in Opportunity Map output. The reason this word is the only filter here is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The block matches only the whole word bane, so any other consultancy name must be added to the pattern or it will appear in output.

summary: Holds the per-deployment brand settings that shared taxonomy code reads, including a filter that blocks certain consultancy names from output.
purpose: Lets each deployment customize its firm and source taxonomy and its branding filter without editing the shared code.
why: The file header says it is per side and that deployments can replace it. The reason beyond that is not stated in the code.
how: The file imports a type from the shared industries file, then exports three values: an empty list of extra firm segments, an empty set of extra taxonomy sources, and a pattern that blocks the word bane. Shared code reads these values when it runs.
inputs: No runtime inputs. The values are typed directly in the file.
outputs: Three exported values used by the shared taxonomy code.
risks: A deployment that does not fill in its own names will publish output with no extra firms and only one blocked word, so other consultancy names could appear. A change in one artifact's copy does not reach the other copy.
debug: If taxonomy output is missing firms or sources, check the brand.ts in the same artifact folder. If a blocked name still appears, check that the pattern matches its spelling.
